requirements.reason: Checkout must derive owner, amount, currency, credit, reservation, PaymentIntent creation, and confirmation identity from locked server state, commit durable checkpoints before Stripe mutations, and release database locks before provider calls.
Payment, provider, booking, reservation, participant, credit, and history state must remain separate, constrained, and updated through one explicit lifecycle matrix.

Late successful payments and capacity conflicts must preserve succeeded payment truth, deny entitlement, and create or reuse one active compensation requirement without executing ad hoc refunds in webhook state application.

Signed Stripe webhooks must be persisted as bounded event envelopes, enqueued atomically into durable jobs, acknowledged only after commit, and processed idempotently from payloads containing only internal event identifiers.

Duplicate, delayed, missing, out-of-order, nonterminal, unknown, failed, canceled, and succeeded PaymentIntent observations must pass through the same canonical transition rules for webhook and targeted reconciliation.
Saved payment methods must be user-owned, provider-verified, idempotent, durable across unknown outcomes, limited to safe metadata, and distinct from paid-waitlist off-session authorization.

This pass must preserve accepted provider-input, transaction-boundary, invariant, SQL/value, migration, authorization, response-minimization, durable-job, community-publish, waitlist, credit, and full-credit checkout compatibility contracts.

Final worker hosting, Stripe sandbox and dashboard evidence, deployed webhook delivery observations, broad scheduled reconciliation, refund and credit-restoration execution, disputes, deployed alerts, and operational runbooks remain later-owned and are not proven by this source-owned pass.
